 Everything you need to know about Aggies-Aztecs clash in San Diego

 Kickoff:  Saturday, 7:30 p.m. MST
 Venue:  Snapdragon Stadium
 TV:  USA Sports
 Radio:  Aggie Sports Network (KZNS 1280 The Zone)
 Series: Saturday’s game will be the 19th meeting between the Aggies and the Aztecs. San Diego State has dominated the head-to-head series, 13-5; however, Utah State is on a three-game winning streak against San Diego State. The Aggies have also won four of the last five matchups. 
 The trends 
 For Utah State: Utah State has played its best football in the past two weeks. The Aggies not only reentered bowl game conversations, but they still have a chance at the Pac-12 championship game after their win over Fresno State last week, but would need help. Even if the Aggies win out, they would need Texas State to lose to either Fresno State or Washington State. 
 Utah State has fully reembraced McCae Hillstead as its starting quarterback after a poor performance and injury to start the year. He hasn’t been lights out, but he’s making enough plays to win games. 
 The biggest boon for the Aggies has been that Hillstead is taking care of the ball. He’s gone back-to-back games without a turnover. His last turnover was an interception against Boise State in early October. 
 Meanwhile, the defense has been downright elite. It has held its last two opponents scoreless in the first half, and hasn’t given up a first-half touchdown since its game against Washington State on Oct. 9. 
 Utah State leads the Pac-12 in fewest opponent yards per game and fewest allowed touchdowns. 
 For San Diego State: The Aztecs are experiencing some eerily similar trends to Utah State. Not only do they have the exact same record, but also have had to rely on two different starting quarterbacks this season. 
 The Aztecs’ senior quarterback, Jayden Denegal, had mixed performances this season. He sustained an injury against Fresno State on Oct. 17, and since then they’ve started freshman Stone Saunders. 
 Saunders has only started two games, took over midway through the Fresno State game and has been inconsistent. He threw for 369 yards against Colorado State, but he was also picked off twice in the loss to the Rams. 
 He then got a win over Washington State, but threw for only 102 yards with an interception and zero touchdowns. San Diego State got the win almost solely in its run game. Lucky Sutton and Javion Kinnard combined for 202 rushing yards and two touchdowns. 
 What to watch for
 Force a one-dimensional offense: Multiple times this year, Utah State has played against quarterbacks that can threaten teams with their legs. That likely won’t be the case Saturday. 
 Saunders has been a pass-only quarterback. In four appearances this year, he has only four rush attempts for minus 9 yards. Two of his four rush attempts were sacks. 
 It would be huge for Utah State to get a handle on its pass coverage because Saunders hasn’t shown an ability to impact the game beyond his passing. 
 If Utah State can do that, then it’ll have San Diego State right where it wants it because of how dominant its run defense has been. 
 1 Comment The Aggies have held their last three opponents to an average of 59 rushing yards per game. San Diego State definitely has shown some ability to run the ball, but Saturday is another prime opportunity for the defense to be lights out. 
 The worst thing Utah State could do is allow explosive plays in the air, which may allow the Aztecs to open things up on the ground. 
 Quotable
 “The identity of the offense is matching and fulfilling the identity of the team to deliver a style of play that gives us our best chance to have success. And so all that’s been discovered, and we’ve adapted and adopted and I’ve shifted to where, while it might not be 40 points a game and setting fireworks off, it’s doing enough to manage the game, to move the ball, to score enough points to help our team win, which is the ultimate goal. I reserve the right as the head coach to try to design those styles on any given year for any given team to give it its best chance. And sometimes that looks different. And today, or this team, it looks a little different right now.” — Utah State coach Bronco Mendenhall 
 “Tremendous opportunity this Saturday against a really good Utah State team. Coach Bronco Mendenhall and his staff are doing a great job. Those guys are playing some great ball. Tremendous opportunity with so much still to play for, obviously with two to play in the conference and obviously flex game to go. Everything’s right out in front of us. None more important than this opportunity against a really, really good defense, an offense that’s finding its identity, and a team that’s playing connected and complementary in all three phases.” — San Diego State coach Sean Lewis
